# An assigned claimant's withdrawal leaves the issue taken

## Context

On 2026-11-16 an outside author closed their own pull request unmerged (#21058, 04:27:48Z) and two seconds later gave the issue back in words on #21016, which the claim responder had assigned to them (comment 6907321144):

> Unclaiming this: I closed #21058 (see the note there). The issue is free for anyone; the branch on that PR has a verified fix plus tests if useful.

The responder ran on that comment (run 43804249017, success) and changed nothing. A maintainer removed the assignment by hand 97 seconds later (the issue's timeline: `unassigned`, actor `neo-gpt-emmy`, 04:29:27Z). It was the first unmerged outside close after the release boundary of #21022 (`NEO_CLAIM_RELEASE_SINCE` = `2026-11-16T00:53:19Z`, read by run 43804246153), so this is the first time the path was exercised by a real contributor.

## The Problem

The responder assigns every first-in-line claimant, so a claimed issue is normally an assigned one. In that state a withdrawal has no effect.

**1. Recognised words change nothing.** Replay of #21016 through `decideClaim` on `dev` `a29510a067`: the issue's real comments and events up to 04:29:00Z, the assignee set, and a newcomer claiming 40 seconds after the withdrawal.

| The assignee's last comment | `isWithdrawal` | The newcomer's decision |
|---|---|---|
| the real sentence above | `false` | `assign: false`, "This one is taken: it's assigned to …" |
| "Please unassign me." | `true` | the same refusal |
| none (control) | n/a | the same refusal |

**2. The withdrawal restarts the hold.** `staleAssignees` counts the 3 days from the assignee's latest comment, so the comment that gives the issue back holds it for 3 more days.

**3. The contributor is told nothing.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` step 3 says how to claim and how long a claim lasts. It names no way to give one back.

The module's tests cover a withdrawal only for a claim that was never assigned (`claimResponse.spec.mjs:225`, an issue without assignees).

## The Architectural Reality

All on `dev` `a29510a067`.

- `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml:511`: an issue comment that is not an outside claim ends the run with "No reply: not an outside contributor claim." The workflow does not import `isWithdrawal`.
- `buildScripts/util/claimResponse.mjs`: `WITHDRAWAL_PATTERNS` (:77) and `isWithdrawal` (:129). `holders` (:454) names a live outside assignee as the holder within `CLAIM_WINDOW_DAYS`. `staleAssignees` (:395) reads the assignee's latest comment or `assigned` event. `isWithdrawal` is consulted for an earlier unassigned claim (`earlierClaim`, :318), in `decideTargetRemoval` (:1085) and in `decidePullRequestRelease` (:1196), never for a current assignee.
- The precedent for an unassign that the module decides and the workflow performs: `decideTargetRemoval` returns `{unassign: true, assignee}` and the workflow's removal step (:402 to :428) calls `removeAssignees`.
- `Design authority:` the module's own JSDoc, "**taken:** a live assignee, an open pull request that resolves the issue, or an earlier unwithdrawn, un-unassigned claimant holds it" (`claimResponse.mjs:13`), and the spec's sentence "a withdrawn claim frees the issue: the next claimant is first in line" (`claimResponse.spec.mjs:225`). A withdrawn claim is meant to hold nothing; the assignment the responder itself adds makes it hold.

## The Fix

1. **The module decides, the workflow acts.** For an issue comment by an outside account that is a current assignee of an open curated issue and reads as a withdrawal, the module returns the assignee to remove and one reply. The workflow removes the assignee, verifies the response as #20750's trap asks, and posts the reply once (a marker, as the claim reply has).
2. **A withdrawn assignee holds nothing.** `holders` and `staleAssignees` stop counting an outside assignee whose latest own comment is a withdrawal. That also covers a failed `removeAssignees` call and a replay.
3. **The reply** says that the issue is free again and how to take it back (`/claim`). If the same author has an open pull request that resolves the issue, the pull request keeps holding it by the existing rule, and the reply says so.
4. **Which words release an assignee.** A release takes an issue away from someone who may still be working, so a deferral must not read as one. Today's readings (`isWithdrawal` on `dev`):

   | Sentence | Today | Must be |
   |---|---|---|
   | the real sentence of 6907321144 | `false` | a release |
   | "I'm withdrawing my claim." | `false` | a release |
   | "Please unassign me." | `true` | a release |
   | "I'm stepping back from this one." | `true` | a release |
   | "Consider it available." | `true` | a release |
   | "Sorry, I can't work on this anymore." | `true` | a release |
   | "I can't finish this before Friday, the PR comes Monday." | `true` | **no** release |
   | "Still working on this." | `false` | no release |

   The implementer chooses the patterns; the table is the contract. A comment that also reads as a claim releases nothing.
5. **`CONTRIBUTING.md` step 3** gets one sentence: how to give a claim back, and that the reply confirms it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: unit tests replay #21016's shape (assignee set, the claim, the bot's reply, the withdrawal, then a newcomer's claim). The newcomer is first in line after the real sentence and after "Please unassign me."; the control without a withdrawal still refuses.
- [ ] AC-2: every row of the table in The Fix (4) is a test with the stated outcome.
- [ ] AC-3: on a withdrawal by an outside assignee the responder removes exactly that assignee and replies once. A second withdrawal comment adds no reply. A team assignee, a non-assignee and a closed or uncurated issue are untouched.
- [ ] AC-4: an assignee whose latest own comment is a withdrawal is no holder and does not restart the 3 days, with the assignment still present (the failed-call case).
- [ ] AC-5: the withdrawing author's open pull request that resolves the issue still holds it, and the reply names it.
- [ ] AC-6: `CONTRIBUTING.md` step 3 says how to give a claim back.
- [ ] AC-7, post-merge, owner `@neo-fable-mnemosyne`: the first real withdrawal by an assigned outside claimant after the merge is linked in #20892's body with the responder's run. No seat can produce it: the responder reads a team account as not outside.

## Out of Scope

- A notice to claimants who were refused while the issue was held. The notice on an unmerged close (`decidePullRequestRelease`) stays as it is; whether a withdrawal needs one is read from #21024's day-14 count of refused claimants.
- A scheduled sweep of silent assignments (#20750's exclusion stands).
- The sibling repositories: they call this workflow at a pinned commit (`neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1764`, `neomjs/neo-agent-institution#989`) and get the change with their next pin.

## Avoided Traps

- **Releasing on every `isWithdrawal` match.** Today a deferral reads as a withdrawal (row 7). That is harmless only because a withdrawal does nothing to an assignee.
- **Curated labels.** None: the workflow writes with the repository's token on `issue_comment` and `pull_request_target`, and its rehearsal runs under that token.
- **A reply to every later comment** by the same account: one reply per release.
